Earth in the south tends to run from light brown to reddish due to high iron content. But it’s still very fertile.

I think I should explain further. Soil in the north of North America is basically alluvial in nature. Largely deposited by glaciers. It’s young soil geologically speaking. Soil in the southern United States is a LOT older and has been highly oxidized giving it a reddish tint. There are rich black and brown deposits, but they are the exception. The soil is still good though. It just isn’t black.
